member.name: T:BeeAppie.Unity.Achievements
member.summary:
Achievements that work offline (docs/plans/21-achievements-offline.md): , and apply at once to a copy kept on the device and are sent in batches, each with the time it happened, when BeeAppie can be reached. reads the copy: the achievements with their wording in the device's language, the progress and the unlock dates, also offline. Nothing here throws.
Sending creates the player, as the other features do, unless the game sends achievements only with consent (a switch in the dashboard): then everything stays on the device until the player allows usage statistics. The UI package shows "Achievement unlocked" by itself (BeeAppieUI.CelebrateAchievements). Client.UnlockAchievementAsync and the other raw calls stay for games that want the server's answer.

member.name: T:BeeAppie.Unity.ChatConnection
member.summary:
Real-time support chat: new messages, typing indicators and conversation changes as they happen, for the conversations you join (and updates about all of the player's own conversations). Messages are still sent with , which pushes them here. Get the shared, connected one with .
Events are raised on the main thread. Messages sent while the connection was down are not replayed: on , fetch what you show again. Not available on WebGL, which has no streaming HTTP.
Under the hood: ASP.NET Core SignalR's JSON protocol over Server-Sent Events, as the Android and iOS SDKs.

Sending creates the player, as submitting a score always has: a leaderboard shows the player's name.
reads a leaderboard and keeps a copy on the device; gives that copy at once (also offline). and do the same for the list of the game's leaderboards. Client.SubmitScoreAsync stays for games that want the server's answer at once.

member.name: T:BeeAppie.Unity.UserData
member.summary: The signed-in player's own data, stored by BeeAppie: small JSON objects under a collection and a key (save slots, progress, settings, unlocked items), the same on all their devices and back after a reinstall. Reads come from the copy on the device, so they work offline; writes apply to it at once and are sent when BeeAppie can be reached. Last write wins. Writes made before the player signs in wait and are sent once they do. Needs the game's "User data" switch in the dashboard and a paid plan. Nothing here throws.
